title: Ex-Post Real Short Rate
revision_note: CPIAUCSL (the seasonally-adjusted CPI leg) is occasionally revised after publication, most often around its annual seasonal-factor update; TB3MS is not revised.

inputs.label: CPI-U, all items, seasonally adjusted (FRED CPIAUCSL)

methodology: This is an EX-POST real rate: it uses realized inflation over the trailing 12 months, not a survey or market measure of expected inflation. It is the actual real return a saver holding 3-month T-bills earned over the prior year - visible only after the fact, not in real time.

real_short_rate[M] = TB3MS[M] - 100 * (CPIAUCSL[M] / CPIAUCSL[M-12] - 1). TB3MS is the 3-month Treasury bill secondary-market rate for month M (FRED, monthly, 1934-01+). The subtracted term is the year-over-year percent change in CPIAUCSL (CPI-U, all items, seasonally adjusted, FRED, monthly, 1947-01+) for the same month M.
Computed at fetch time in Python from the two FRED legs, the same pattern as scripts/fetch_spreads.py - there is no precomputed 'real short rate' series on FRED.

A month is emitted only when both legs are computable for it - TB3MS[M] exists, and both CPIAUCSL[M] and CPIAUCSL[M-12] exist so the YoY change is defined. No forward-fill, no interpolation across a gap.
The YoY CPI leg needs twelve months of CPI history behind it, so the series can only start 1948-01 (twelve months after CPI's own 1947-01 start), well after TB3MS's own 1934-01 start.
notes: Values are percentage points (a reading of -3.00 means the real rate was -3.00% that year), not a decimal fraction.

Three episodes stand out: deeply negative real rates through 1948, when postwar inflation ran far ahead of a still-pegged T-bill yield (-9.27pp in January 1948); the negative real rates of the mid-to-late 1970s, when T-bill yields lagged accelerating inflation (-5.71pp in February 1975); and the swing to strongly positive real rates in the early 1980s under the Volcker Fed's disinflation (+6.88pp in August 1983). The series cannot reach the wartime 1940s at all: CPIAUCSL starts 1947-01 and the year-over-year leg needs twelve months behind it, so 1948-01 is the first month that exists. Note that 1949 is strongly positive, not negative — consumer prices fell that year.

October 2025 is missing from this series, and that is correct: BLS cancelled the CPI release for that month during the 2025 government shutdown, so CPIAUCSL goes straight from 2025-09 to 2025-11 and no real rate can be computed for October. The month is omitted rather than interpolated; the chart line connects across the one-month break.
TB3MS is not seasonally adjusted; CPIAUCSL is. Neither leg is smoothed or averaged beyond FRED's own published monthly figures.

presentation.summary: The 3-month Treasury bill rate minus the trailing year-over-year change in CPI - the realized (ex-post) real return a saver earned holding short-term Treasuries, back to 1948.
